reviews.text: I played the demo and was instantly hooked with the gunplay and gun customization. I was worried the game would be a little too easy from the demo but the full game has proved me wrong. for 20 bucks I highly recommend this. I can see myself getting at least 40 hours out of this, beats getting a 20 dollar fast food meal and bad gas

Edit: I left this initial review on launch day... within a few hours, devs already released a patch that addresses basically all of my complaints except for the enemy AI simplistically always just running straight towards you. I can't say I've ever left a negative review and flipped it to positive within such a short span of time. Game is both less grindy and difficulty now seems to be about in line with what I'd expect in the genre. Original review: === Too grindy at launch. Hopefully it will improve. I've played a lot of roguelite FPS games over the years (Gunfire Reborn, Roboquest, Battle Shapers, Aftershock, Deadzone Rogue, Immortal Redneck, to name a few), and none of those had me bounce off this quickly. The level of grind that seems to be presented here seems rather extreme. Granted, I have only done 1 of the starter difficulty and two on the default difficulty, but I unlocked nearly no meta-progress at all on either of my normal difficulty attempts, and not really that much beating the starter. The difficulty gulf between starter and normal difficulty is also crazy high... I can't get past more than a few rooms on normal difficulty. That's not really so unusual for roguelites, except this game seems to have no way to raise your HP/shields permanently like other similar FPS roguelites. So it's never going to get easier. Yeah, you can perma-upgrade your guns. But it feels like I'm stuck with unfun guns unless I get enough currency to unlock better ones... which would require a fair amount of grinding based on my initial hour of play (counting the demo). I'd also say that the enemies in the game are not the most exciting to fight against (compared to other roguelite FPSs, they just always run straight at you.) Currently considering whether to refund or not, but I'll wait until a few patches drop first (assuming that happens during Steam's refund window).

[h1]《Galactic Vault》简评[/h1] 这款第一人称射击游戏，以肉鸽构筑的形式，带来一场绝对令玩家肾上腺素飙升的快节奏刺激战斗。每一个普通战斗的房间，玩家都将面临潮水般袭来的敌人，每一次Boss战斗，玩家都会面对各种不同机制的Boss。有一说一，本作拿着枪械疯狂突突突的感觉爽倒是爽了，但是构筑成型面对一堆小怪和强力Boss的高难度挑战所带来的无力感也是真的好憋屈。如果游戏能够在经历一番磨难之后，享受到割草无双或者毁灭战士的快乐，那就最好了。 [h1]剧情设定[/h1] 玩家扮演一名来自前VOLT（密库行动和失落科技，Vault Operations & Lost Tech）的特工，为了拿到被企业寡头所垄断的科技技术，于是潜入到该企业的科技库中，将所有科技洗劫一空，充实自家的武器库，以面对越来越难的战斗。 [h1]基础玩法[/h1] 其基础玩法为第一人称射击游戏，对着敌人突突突的那种。玩家对战时，可以使用普通射击、倍镜射击、近战攻击、手雷投掷、特殊技能以及跳跃、下蹲等操作，这些内容没有特别复杂的机制，基本就是很常见的带有简单动作的射击游戏。不过，游戏地图的设计倒是有些东西，玩家面对数量贼多的敌人，无法站在一处有利地形站桩输出，必须得游走八方、上蹿下跳、左右挪移，本作地图设计得很好，就提供了这么一个走位的条件，地形方面有一点不足之处在于全部房间的地形貌似重复度非常高，每一次战斗都对地形似曾相似。 [h1]肉鸽构筑[/h1] 不过，很传统线性闯关制的第一人称射击游戏不同，本作选择了肉鸽战斗的机制。即随机房间路线的选择、随机构筑体系配件的搭配。玩家每闯过一个房间，就可以选择一次随机奖励，这些奖励包括护符、枪械核心、弹匣、枪口、子弹、瞄具、手雷、物品等等配件，一路杀下去，直到最终的Boss房间，角色自然获得的奖励越多，综合实力也就越来越强，构筑体系包括的内容非常丰富，但是玩家获得奖励的次数有限，所以如何来选择这些奖励，再结合角色的技能和强化等内容，将各种升级奖励组合起来，生成史诗级组合，实现惊人的效果，达成策略性的武器构建，这是本作想要通关的关键。 [h1]挑战难度[/h1] 然而，实际战斗体验和理想中的很不一样。理想的战斗，乌拉乌拉乌拉，咱越战越勇、越战越强，一众敌人全是插标卖首之徒，不堪一击。实际的战斗，一群敌人四面八方冲过来，挡不住根本挡不住，蚁多咬死象之典型。尤其是有些关卡的任务目标不仅仅是击杀全部的敌人，还有房间是需要玩家占领点位之类的，全部点位占领前无限刷敌不说，玩家还必须蹲守点位没法移动，这可太不简单了。至于Boss，各种各样的机制都有，有各种召唤小弟的，有频繁无敌放技能的，有范围攻击难躲避的，反正就是历尽千辛万苦打到Boss房间，依旧要面临更难的挑战。有一说一，角色不断战斗、奖励、构筑得到的提升，应该是越到后面玩的越爽，但是本作的高难度挑战，只能说有刺激、有热血、有磨砺唯独不太爽。 [h1]最后[/h1] 喜欢快节奏、很刺激、超热血，喜欢带有构筑成长的肉鸽类，喜欢高难度挑战自我技术的玩家，可以试试本作。 [quote] 闲暇时光，不妨试试游戏。 欢迎关注[url=store.steampowered.com/curator/45653622/] 闲暇時光鉴赏组 [/url] [/quote]

Updating review: I am at a point where I am forcing myself to play out of principle of purchase but it's lacking in content and the progression does not feel rewarding. The maps are boring, objectives boring, and the environments and enemies are all the same (some with more health than others). Choices mid run don't feel rewarding enough, and the choices outside of run for the skill tree are way too slow and non-meaningful. I am trying to enjoy it but I regret the purchase for now. Will wait to see what the developer does. Does not hold a candle to the games I mentioned below. Needs more time in the oven to warrant it's price. ____________________________ Very early impressions tell me the game will be worth the asking price if the devs continue working on it, it's very fun and reminiscent of Deadzone: Rogue, Deadlink, and VOID/BREAKER, but - it's over priced right now for the content and palette. It's more of a $10-$15 game - it gets very repetitive and samey-samey quick, enemy and environmental wise (gunplay and gameplay are fine for this genre). The mods concept behind different doors is cool and so far has been engaging, I have not played enough to tell what the long term viability of the builds will be. I am only recommending the game as not to hurt the developer review score. I enjoy these types of games so much that it doesn't bother me I spent the money, but it's may not be worth the asking price right now to most people.

I have very mixed feelings about this game. It’s definitely a better FPS than a roguelite. The gunplay feels good, the color identity is very well executed, and the fact that our weapon changes visually when we buy upgrades adds a nice touch to the game. My first impressions were very positive, but the longer I play, the more flaws and limitations I start to notice. 1. Melee upgrade in the attachment upgrade room I have to admit that I practically never use melee, because the range, speed, and damage don’t really encourage me to do so. Not to mention the melee upgrades themselves, which didn’t really add much to my runs. A separate room dedicated to melee upgrades would be a much better solution. 2. Shared reroll price Considering how slowly the economy builds up in this game, having a shared reroll cost between rooms makes rerolling become not really worth it after a short while, especially given the types of upgrades available (more on that later). Shop pricing is also too high. 3. Quality and quantity of upgrades I got the impression that the developers intentionally tried to prevent the player from becoming too overpowered, which in my opinion (especially on the hardest difficulty where hordes of enemies rush you) is a mistake for this type of game. Upgrades like reduced magazine size that grows with each enemy killed are interesting, but something like a small damage boost at the cost of not being able to move forward while shooting because it's pushing you backwards feels like overkill. If it could be used in some kind of Jetpack Joyride–style gameplay, it might actually increase the fun factor, but unfortunately that’s not the case. There are too few upgrades that allow a run to feel truly unique, and too many that simply increase damage or firerate by a percentage without adding any additional effects. In my opinion, the game should allow for more abstract combinations where, through the right upgrades, a player could turn a shotgun into something that essentially functions like a one-chamber sniper rifle. Yes, there is an upgrade that makes your weapon fire a shotgun-like spread instead of a single projectile, but from my experience that upgrade ruined runs more often than it defined them. 4. A wall of text that doesn’t say much Addon descriptions are very often presented as long blocks of text, but they rarely clearly explain what they actually do. What is Luck? What is weapon handling (especially considering that, by default, weapons have almost no recoil or bullet spread)? Why not add icons and provide a detailed description when hovering over a given upgrade? This would speed up the item selection process (fast-paced games need to maintain their tempo somehow). An additional option could be a question mark icon next to each stat in the menu that explains how it works. 5. Price to Quality This is the studio’s first game, and there are several oversights for example, enemies sometimes spawn in the hall the player is leaving, which causes them to get stuck behind the door and makes them impossible to kill (blocking the ability to complete the room). There’s also a default project Unity background scene visible in one of the rooms. In its current state, in terms of both content and quality, if the game had released as early access I probably wouldn’t have had an issue and would have had much higher expectations for its future, but since it’s a full release at full price, I’m approaching it much more critically. 10$ could be much better choice for many reasons. 6. Variety The activities within the rooms themselves are quite decent, capturing a point, shooting cargo, fighting waves, or clearing a room, but I definitely feel there’s a lack of greater variety in the rooms or their types. A few platforming elements, environmental hazards, or boss arenas could have more variants, because right now it feels like I’m doing the same thing and same places every time. The enemies are quite generic and don’t stand out much, aside from a few exceptions. That would be fine if the game (as I mentioned earlier) focused more on greater variety in each run by progression. I realy want this game to be "my next balatro" but there is just not enough content (or content is not that well exectued) to be there. I hope that devs will improve this game in future, I really do, it could be realy fun, but just not yet.
Good game, just not worth full price.

I want to like the game, I like Dead zone rouge which I think it's very similar to. My problem with this game is the progression. Like a lot of games I've played lately. the progression is too slow. I have literally hundreds of games to play, and if I don't feel like the time I've invested in a game is rewarded somehow I will play something else. .I'm not some middle schooler who has 16 hours a day to grind to level up. I play a few hours a day and if I'm not progressing in my levels and gaining new skills and options. I'm not going to continue playing the game. It's just not fun to play. In it's current state this is a thumbs down for me, 2/5.

这个游戏总体感觉还行，虽然说画面和敌人的样子感觉一般，感觉就是那种素材库的那种素材，但是体验感拉满了，能让你明显地感觉到肉鸽射击类游戏带来的爽感，比我之前体验的同样类型的深渊之巢要好玩不少。游戏武器有5种大类，每个大类的武器又有不同的武器样式。肉鸽元素分局内和局外的，局内的也分很多种，包括枪上各种配件的提升，还有手雷护肤等其他要素的肉鸽，最让我感觉爽的，就是他的技能，有一个飞行背包的技能，能在空中飞8秒，配上我那个能爆炸的子弹，真成法鸡了有没有懂的？而且几种技能不冲突。局外的话就是根据你在局内用的武器给熟练度，然后武器会有等级，武器升级就可以在局外根据自己的需要加点。这个游戏确实好玩，推荐给喜欢玩肉鸽FPS的玩家。 [quote]欢迎关注 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45531068/]黑白测评[/url] [hr]黑夜显真 白昼辨伪

Well the game is fun when it works. However the game constantly freezes and most of the time it freezes when I’m in the boss fight or when I’m changing settings. So I have to restart in order to fix the issue and it doesn’t save my changes to settings so I have to change settings again and hope it doesn’t freeze and it when I am able to change my settings without the game freezing it never saves my settings so I always have to change them back whenever I start the game up. Lots of the upgrades don’t work half the time. They do nothing or maybe they will do something it’s 50/50 if it’s going to do what it’s supposed to do. The game also stutters and lags every once in a while. Enemies and my character gets stuck on the environment all the time. This game has to many issues to be worth it. Progression seems very slow as well but that might also just be because I’m constantly having to restart the game and my runs freeze all the time so I can’t complete them to get currencies for permanent upgrades. I’ve also uninstalled and reinstalled the game many times and done everything I can to try and fix the issues and nothing works.

76原价其实有点贵，如果不是纯富哥建议至少打五折再入手。 多玩了几把发现时长其实差不多够的，并不是之前我评论时说的一局较短。 个人挑刺感觉选择选项的框不是很清晰，受伤反馈不够，敌人也不是非常明显（但是头顶有条显示剩余敌人在哪个方向倒不错），然后我玩霰弹枪给我匹一个飞天boss也很抽象 但别的都很舒服，手感不差，新鲜度还是有的。 后续要是有持续更新并且能打五折真可以入，现在推荐只是觉得这游戏底子不错。

Although the Gimmicky projectile bouncing and other fun build ideas are cool here, I was able to beat the first 3 difficulties no deaths. Then I have to replay the third difficulty (which i already beat) 3 more times to Play the custom difficulty or anything harder/different. No real challenge here which makes the choices seem meaningless in the run. Might be better with some later content but it's a no from me for now.

[h3]RANKING:[/h3] [table] [tr] [td] [h3][strike]AVOID | FLAWED | MAYBE[/strike] | [b]WORTHWHILE[/b] | [strike]COMPELLING | UNMISSABLE [/strike] [/h3] [/td] [/tr] [/table] [h3]SYNOPSIS:[/h3] [table] [tr] [th][b]ASSESSMENT:[/b][/th] [/tr] [tr] [td] Galactic Vault is a solid FPS roguelite with fluid gunplay defined by a myriad of weapon-based mechanics that allow for multiple playstyles. Sharp controls provide precision movement & aiming. RNG influenced session upgrades are a mix of routine augments that bear fruit when correctly synergised. While a few fun, OP abilities possess a wow factor that makes them necessary choices on tougher runs. Some offerings can be mitigated with re-rolls. Grindy meta-progression provides longevity & grants leeway to invest in alternate weapon styles, which lifts blander weapons to an acceptable level. Not all of which fit the futuristic setting. While replay value is high, levels need stronger randomisation & derivative enemies need expanding to dampen a repetitive experience. More weapons & upgrades to offer true build alternates are needed too. Already provides a [b]WORTHWHILE[/b] experience. [/td] [/tr] [/table] [table] [tr] [td][b]STATUS:[/b][/td] [td]Fully released & currently being supported, see Roadmap [/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]APPEAL:[/b][/td] [td]Fans of stat-influenced FPS with short runs in a roguelite format [/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][b]VALUE:[/b][/td] [td]With more weapons, upgrades, enemies & level randomisation, the full price would be spot on [/td] [/tr] [/table] [quote=]Key provided by developer through [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/32732116-IndieGems/][b]INDIEGEMS[/b][/url] curator | Check out their vids on [url=https://www.youtube.com/@IndieGems2][b]YOUTUBE[/b][/url][/quote] [i]More info below....[/i] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3698027131 [h3]HIGHLIGHTS:[/h3] 🟡 GUNPLAY is fast-paced. As difficulty scales, clearing waves sways from too easy to satisfying with the right combination of upgrades. Mechanics allow for camping, kiting, strafing, jumping (or hovering) depending on the map, weapon, upgrades & situation. Hip-fire or ADS are both viable & even preferable depending on the choices made. 🟡 MECHANICS offers different playstyles. Movement speed enables kiting &/or strafing to avoid damage. Rate of fire, range, ammo capacity & reload impact weapons. Elemental effects, weak points, piercing munitions, explosive effects, dividing or fragmenting bullets & gravity amplify or affect damage. Knife melee, unlimited bullets & breaking manual reload provides alternate pathways to reloading or the need to pick-up ammo. Stacking shield & health regeneration raise survivability chances. 🟡 UPGRADES come in x7 weapon focused categories. Covering an insane range of enhancements; a mix of all rounders, situational & playstyle. Some are underwhelming. Others impactful & balanced. A few are OP & fun as hell. Stacking the right weaker upgrades keeps many of them relevant & useful depending on weapon & playstyle. 🟡 FOES come as 15x types of regular mobs, many are derivative. Drones are standout in several melee & ranged forms. Humanoids are a mix of chargers, melee, riflemen, snipers & mortars. Mortars are annoying as hell being able to snap-shot accurately at close range. Turret variants aren't distinct enough. Bosses deliver surprisingly engaging battles as they are difficult to overcome until understanding attack patterns. 🟡 AI behaviour is convincing as drones swarm, snipers crouch next to cover, riflemen strafe & mortars reposition. Suicide drone bombers & chargers that home in on the player after they move are particularly nasty. 🟡 Great REPLAY VALUE comes from a combination of maps, objectives, wave spawns, weapons & potential builds. At the cost of repetitive gameplay from a single mode with only x2 difficulties, limited attack wave configurations & x9 unique rooms that are not duplicated on shorter runs. Augmented by a custom run mode. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3691010899 [h3]OFF TARGET:[/h3] ⚪ Well made LEVELS offer basic variety from map-size, alternating victory objectives, high ground & to a lesser degree enemy entry points & useable cover. Jump points & explosive barrels add additional tactical elements. Randomising certain décor & other tactical elements would reduce the feeling of over-familiarity. ⚪ ATMOSPHERE looks futuristic, but visuals are too sanitised. Dirty textures would give it a lived in feel. Bosses are brought to life with varied animations, that shows them behaving distinctly. Much of the audio is serviceable. Weapons would sound better with ballistic sounds that mirror upgrades. Hitting weak points sounds particularly satisfying. ⚪ META-PROGRESSION is fairly meaningful. Revolving around weapon types, but is not deep with only x10 categories to invest up to x30 points earned in. Will take a few dozen hours to max investment. Achieving challenge & mastery milestones provides additional skill-points, but is grindy. Investment points can be reset at no cost. ⚪ CHALLENGE from the 15x types of regular mobs scales well with longer runs. Elite mobs appear with greater health, shields, faster movement & shoot rates. Boss fights are engaging, with varied attack patterns that makes them difficult to overcome without being spongy. ⚪ SPECIAL ABILITIES a mix of satisfying & underwhelming alternate fire options. RNG does not mitigate the choice on offer during a run. Perhaps linked to the weapon chosen for the run. Along with those for weapons, extra bells & whistles can make the player's slide & jump abilities more tactical in their use. The need to hold down two keys for combos can be confusing. ⚪ Fair LONGEVITY comes from meta-progression. Unlocking custom mode offers a little more control over which enemies & which of rooms will be faced, up to x20. As does unlocking weapons of which there arent enough to use a surplus of credits earned from runs. ⚪ PRODUCTION needs more content across the board & QoL to expand existing features to increase variety & lower repetitiveness. Its already polished & well optimised. Apart from x1 CTD experienced in custom mode after 25h, stability was perfect. Others report the game freezing. Bugs experienced were minor. A few reported by others continues to trickle in. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3698007257 [h3]SHORTCOMINGS:[/h3] 🟤 WEAPONS are vanilla platforms for upgrades. Some are more fun than others. Differences in basic models come from rate-of-fire. Other stats contribute to 'preferred playstyles' Sidearms & ARs are too similar in appearance. Only the railgun fits the futuristic setting. 🟤 MISSING FEATURES for feasible addition include: no endless mode for endurance runs. Can't lock upgrade choices with credits to mitigate RNG further. Needs optional [randomised] room starting parameters &, randomisation of room décor & layout to changeup the experience. There is no coop. 🟤 ANNOYANCES include rare instances where the choice of two identical upgrades appear. Having to use two key combination to execute the slide ability. [h2]This Isn't It[/h2] I’ve noticed a lot of discussion around Galactic Vault, especially with oddly enough... A lot of people claiming it rivals or even surpasses Dead Zone Rogue. As if. From my experience, Galactic Vault attempts to capture a similar atmosphere, but it ultimately feels like a less modest, more expensive version in the genre. A significant factor is its reliance on the Synty asset kit, which, while visually functional, gives the game a familiar look that’s been seen in numerous other indie projects. Think of any game with the "Generic" noob character or purchase. After spending about an hour with the demo, I could see some potential. While it doesn’t quite reach the heights of Dead Zone Rogue or Void Breaker, two much cheaper alternatives with greater weapon builds and depth, the weapon crafting system is a notable feature that could have helped it carve out its own identity. However, upon the full release, I found that not much had changed. Most weapons remain locked aside from the SMG, and upgrades, earned through rather unchallenging enemy AI, offer minor improvements, such as a 1% increase in weapon stats, all tied to individual weapon progression. For example, after nearly two hours of gameplay, I reached level 7 with the SMG, unlocking only a slight damage boost and minimal recoil reduction. These changes felt insignificant, especially since recoil and gun feedback don’t have much impact due to the game’s current design. Weapons like have unexpectedly high rates of fire, and overall, most guns feel overly stable, lacking the responsive feel that makes a shooter stand out as you mag dump every second. [h2]Conclusion[/h2] Galactic Vault is a disappointing entry in the indie game landscape, offering little more than recycled assets and uninspired design. While some may find fleeting enjoyment, the lack of originality, shallow gameplay, and uninventive mechanics make it difficult to recommend, especially when there are superior alternatives at a similar or even lower price point. For those familiar with the genre more specifically the assets, will notice the game’s shortcomings, as its attempt to mimic better titles. Ultimately, Galactic Vault is an example of how important it is for indie games to carve out their own identity, rather than rely on cheap assets to make a game faster, especially when it's their first game. It's good enough to be fun, but not good enough to really recommend in my opinion, this game kind of has that early access type feel to it. It's hard to not compare this one to others competing in the same genre, but I will say that this one has pretty above average gunplay in comparison. Though it's severely lacking in the audio department. Visuals are fine, though I find myself shooting a door frame sometimes due to the lights looking the same as the HP bars above enemies. Boss animations seem kind of clunky and give off placeholder vibes, in both the boss intro and for instance the lizard's stomp animation. Basically all boss attacks are dodgable by just walking in a straight line, providing little challenge. Unlockable weapons are pretty much straight upgrades to whatever came before, crippling variety. Speaking of variety, all builds basically come down to the same bounce/split/explosive/elemental, there's no firemode gimmicks, no upgrades to a gun's base abilities, or audio feedback for triggering percentage based ammo types. About 80% through most runs you don't have to aim anymore due to the monsoon of bullet splitting or explosives (or both) you're pumping out, and it kinda ruins the one thing this game has over it's colleagues in the genre, the gunplay. At it's full price prob skip it for now, unless you're really hungry for one of these roguelike fpses.

Overall, a great shooter if you wanna just... get lost blowing up enemies for a couple hours and relax. Just put on some music and blow up some bots. Minor gripe, shotguns felt weak. Interestingly enough, shotguns got a tweak in the last patch, so hopefully they hit with a good impact now,

Pretty fun game. Barebones but scratches that roguelike itch where you just want to keep doing another run. Certain movement mechanics like jetpack, dashes, etc are skills you can only acquire mid run so lots of variability in how the runs feel. I usually like to do that for fast paced games to get more frames.

Received for free. Thank you devs. Galactic Vault is a roguelite FPS inspired in games like Roboquest and Deadzone Rogue where you launch yourself into ships and have to go through waves to reach the final boss of the vault. Unironically enough, this game has infinite choices of weapon variety with the Charms system, in which you quite literally slap a charm in your weapon and it slowly gets tuned out. You also have the crafting system to craft the few weapons this game has and experiment with everything in your base. Speaking of base, your hub is your own personal vessel. Here you can change difficulty, weapons and etc. Playtime between runs is also great for thoose who cant handle 5/6 worlds and complex BS from a traditional roguelike, Galactic Vault actually plays better than some more known ones. This is quite the polished game and is receiving content here and there after it launched and i heavily recommend buying it. If 20 bucks is too much for you, Steam has a refund option.

Are you thinking about buying this game? If yes, then you should get it - full price or otherwise. During my first hour of playing this I was having an amazing time, after the second I was miserable. The difficulty is all over the place, some guns like the shot guns feel like a trap because some bosses just don't seem to take damage properly from them and the unlock system is just awful. I honestly cant see me unlocking any of the other classes in a reasonable amount of time because some of the requirements are ludicrous or just pure luck based, and the rate at which you get credits is wayyyyy too slow. I'll come back to this one after a bit and see what's been fixed, but right now I cant really recommend it.

Having a lot of fun so far, definitely scratches that FPS Roguelite itch and it's fast-paced enough without being unintelligible nonsense. My one point of feedback so far is, ironically enough, a lack of damage feedback on the player. It doesn't need to be anything over the top, but I feel there needs to be a bit more visual feedback when you get hit. I often find myself locked in, scooting around on my buttcheeks and blasting robots and won't even realize I'm almost dead until I look down at my health, which gets a lot more important on the higher difficulties. Other than that, having a blast.
